**Given Data:**
- Resistance, $R = 10\text{ }\Omega$
- Capacitance, $C = 200\text{ }\mu\text{F} = 200 \times 10^{-6}\text{ F}$
- Voltage, $V = 250\text{ V}$
- Frequency, $f = 50\text{ Hz}$

**Calculations:**
1. **Capacitive Reactance ($X_c$):**
   $$X_c = \frac{1}{2\pi f C} = \frac{1}{2 \pi \times 50 \times 200 \times 10^{-6}} = 15.915\text{ }\Omega$$

2. **Impedance ($Z$):**
   $$Z = R - jX_c = 10 - j15.915
   \Rightarrow |Z| = \sqrt{10^2 + (15.915)^2} = 18.79\text{ }\Omega$$

(i) **Circuit Current ($I$):**
$$I = \frac{V}{|Z|} = \frac{250}{18.79} = 13.305\text{ A}$$

(ii) **Power Factor ($\cos\phi$):**
$$\cos\phi = \frac{R}{|Z|} = \frac{10}{18.79} = 0.532\text{ (leading)}$$

(iii) **Active Power ($P$):**
$$P = V I \cos\phi = 250 \times 13.305 \times 0.532 = 1769.4\text{ W} = 1.769\text{ kW}$$

(iv) **Reactive Power ($Q$):**
$$Q = V I \sin\phi = 250 \times 13.305 \times \sin(57.87^\circ) = 2810.6\text{ VAR} = 2.81\text{ kVAR}$$.
proTip: Remember that capacitive circuits always have a leading power factor. Clearly specify 'leading' or 'lagging' alongside the power factor value.
